name: Spanakorizo (Greek Spinach and Rice)

ingredients.name: olive oil, plus more for serving
mature spinach, a mixture, with stems

instructions.primary_message: Chop the yellow onion. Roughly chop the garlic. Rinse the medium-grain brown rice. Roughly chop the mature spinach.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 medium yellow onion
2 cloves garlic
1 cup medium-grain brown rice
14 oz mature spinach, a mixture, with stems

instructions.primary_message: In a large, heavy-bottomed pot, heat 4 tablespoons olive oil over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add onion and 1 teaspoon salt, and cook until onion is translucent, about 7 minutes. Add garlic, oregano, tomato paste, and miso (if using), and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute. Add rice and stir well until rice is coated with oil mixture and smells slightly toasted, about 1 minute.
Stir in broth plus remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil to combine. Cover and bring to a boil.

Add greens and 1/2 teaspoon salt and stir to combine. Cover and bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to medium-low to maintain a simmer and cook until rice is cooked through and liquid has mostly absorbed, but is still slightly viscous, 40 to 45 minutes.
Let rice sit off heat with lid slightly ajar for an additional 10 minutes. Serve warm or at room temperature with a drizzle of olive oil and lemon wedges.

schema_metadata.keywords: Spanakorizo, Greek Spinach and Rice Recipe

description: Spanakorizo is an easy, filling Greek spinach-and-rice dish cooked in olive oil and broth until tender and lightly saucy. Perfect as a vegetarian main or hearty side.
notes:
Optional or for serving: 2 tablespoons white miso paste (optional); Lemon wedges for garnish

Optional substitutions: homemade chicken broth → vegetable stock or store-bought low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth; mature spinach → similar dark greens

Notes: If using white rice, reduce the broth to 1 1/2 cups and begin checking for doneness around 20 minutes. Brown rice will need the full 2 cups of broth and about 40 to 45 minutes. Wild rice blends may require up to 2 1/2 cups of broth and closer to 45 minutes—consult the package instructions and adjust as needed.

Make-ahead and storage: Leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days.
author: Sharon Brenner
